title: Shock, Immunity and Allergy: The PCP's Why

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already spot shock, give oxygen, and give IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis. Today, as a PCP:

  1. What shock does inside the cell, and how the four types differ
  2. How immunity and inflammation work, and how allergy becomes anaphylaxis
  3. What the PCP adds in the BC anaphylaxis protocol

Textbook: Chapter 6, PDF pages 378–429
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson we followed water, salt and acid; today we use that on the sickest patients. As an EMR you already spot shock, give oxygen, and give intramuscular epinephrine for anaphylaxis. As a PCP, you also decide whether to give fluid, how much, and when to stop, and you carry new drugs. To decide well, you need the why. Today we cover three things: what shock does inside the cell and how the four types differ, how immunity and inflammation work and how an allergy becomes anaphylaxis, and what the PCP adds in the BC anaphylaxis protocol.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课我们追踪了水、盐和酸，今天把这些知识用在最危重的病人身上。作为 EMR，你已经会识别休克、给氧，也会给过敏性休克病人肌注肾上腺素。作为 PCP，你还要决定给不给液体、给多少、何时停，而且手里多了新药。要做好决定，就得懂原理。今天讲三件事：休克在细胞里造成什么、四种休克有何不同；免疫和炎症怎样运作、过敏怎样变成过敏性休克；以及 BC 过敏性休克流程里 PCP 多做什么。

slides.title: Inside the shocked cell
slides.body:
perfusion drops→cells work without oxygen→lactic acid, little energy
  • Result: metabolic acidosis, swollen cells, leaking enzymes
  • Stress hormones push blood glucose up
  • The same cell damage in every type of shock

If shock lasts: MODS — lungs, kidneys, liver and clotting fail together, hours to days later. Death rate 60–90%.
slides.say: Let's look inside the shocked cell. When perfusion drops, cells don't get enough oxygen, so they switch to anaerobic metabolism, which means making energy without oxygen. It's like a generator on bad fuel: little power, lots of exhaust. The exhaust is lactic acid, so the patient slides into metabolic acidosis, one reason a shocked patient breathes fast. With little energy, cells swell and leak. Stress hormones push the glucose up. And if shock lasts, several organs can fail together, hours to days later. This is MODS, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, and sixty to ninety percent of these patients die.
slides.sayZh: 我们看看休克时细胞里面的情况。灌注下降时，细胞得不到足够的氧，就转为无氧代谢，也就是不靠氧气产生能量。就像发电机烧劣质燃料：电力少、废气多。废气就是乳酸，病人于是滑向代谢性酸中毒，这也是休克病人呼吸快的原因之一。能量不足，细胞就肿胀、渗漏。应激激素会让血糖升高。如果休克持续，几小时到几天后多个器官会一起衰竭，这叫 MODS，多器官功能障碍综合征，死亡率百分之六十到九十。

slides.title: Four types of shock
slides.body:
TypeWhat failsExamples
Cardiogenicthe pumpMI with ≥ 40% of muscle lost
Obstructiveflow is blockedtamponade, tension pneumothorax, large PE
Hypovolemicvolume is lostbleeding, vomiting, diarrhea
Distributivevessels too wideanaphylaxis, sepsis, neurogenic

Central = cardiogenic + obstructive · Peripheral = hypovolemic + distributive. Fluid refills an empty tank; it can't fix a weak pump or a blocked pipe.
slides.say: The book sorts shock into central and peripheral. Central shock is a problem of the heart or great vessels: cardiogenic, when the pump fails, usually after a heart attack destroys forty percent or more of the muscle; or obstructive, when flow is blocked, as in cardiac tamponade, a tension pneumothorax or a large pulmonary embolism. Peripheral shock is a volume or vessel problem: hypovolemic, from bleeding, vomiting or diarrhea; or distributive, when vessels open too wide, as in anaphylaxis, sepsis or a spinal cord injury. Here's why a PCP must name the type: fluid refills an empty tank, but it can't repair a weak pump or clear a blocked pipe.
slides.sayZh: 书里把休克分为中枢性和外周性。中枢性是心脏或大血管的问题：心源性，就是泵衰竭，通常是心梗毁掉了百分之四十以上的心肌；或梗阻性，就是血流被堵，比如心包填塞、张力性气胸或大面积肺栓塞。外周性是容量或血管的问题：低血容量性，来自出血、呕吐或腹泻；或分布性，就是血管扩得太开，比如过敏性休克、脓毒症或脊髓损伤。PCP 必须先分清类型，原因在于：液体能把空油箱加满，却修不好无力的泵，也疏通不了堵住的管道。

slides.title: Reading perfusion on scene
slides.body:
• Peripheral pulses: present? strong? (cold, obesity can fool you)
  • Capillary refill > 2 s, mottling, pallor → poor skin perfusion
  • Mental status = brain perfusion
  • Pulse fast in most shock, but not fast in neurogenic shock
  • Book: some studies aim for systolic ≈ 80 while bleeding continues
  • BC: bolus 20 mL/kg (max 2 L), reassess every 500 mL
slides.say: On scene, feel the peripheral pulses: are they there, and are they strong? Cold weather and obesity can fool you. Capillary refill should be under two seconds; a longer refill, with mottled or pale skin, means poor skin perfusion. Mental status tells you about the brain. Most shock speeds the pulse up, but neurogenic shock gives low pressure with a pulse that is slow, or at least not fast. About fluids: the book mentions studies aiming for a systolic of about eighty while bleeding continues. For the BC exam, give twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, and recheck these signs every five hundred.
slides.sayZh: 在现场，先摸外周脉搏：有没有？有没有力？寒冷和肥胖会骗你。毛细血管再充盈应少于两秒；更长，再加上皮肤花斑或苍白，说明皮肤灌注差。神志反映大脑的灌注。大多数休克脉搏会变快，但神经源性休克是低血压配上偏慢、至少不快的脉搏。关于补液：书里提到有研究主张在持续出血时把收缩压维持在八十左右。BC 考试按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复查一遍这些指标。

slides.q: A man fell from a roof and can't move his legs. BP 80/50, pulse 52, skin warm and dry. Which shock is most likely, and what should you expect?
options: Hypovolemic — a bolus will quickly fix the pressure
Neurogenic — the pressure may not respond well to fluid
Compensated shock — no treatment is needed
slides.say: Let's practise. A man fell from a roof and can't move his legs. His blood pressure is eighty over fifty, his pulse is fifty-two, and his skin is warm and dry. Which shock is most likely, and what should you expect? A, hypovolemic; a bolus will quickly fix the pressure. B, neurogenic; the pressure may not respond well to fluid. C, cardiogenic; start CPAP right away. D, compensated shock; no treatment is needed. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来练一练。一名男子从屋顶摔下，双腿不能动。血压八十比五十，脉搏五十二，皮肤温暖干燥。最可能是哪种休克？你应该预料到什么？A，低血容量性，推注补液会很快把血压纠正；B，神经源性，血压可能对补液反应不好；C，心源性，马上上 CPAP；D，代偿期休克，不需要处理。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Low pressure with a slow pulse and warm, dry skin after a spinal injury is the classic neurogenic picture: the vessels lose their tone and open wide, so fluid often doesn't fix it. Still look for hidden bleeding, because a trauma patient can have both. A ignores the slow pulse and warm skin. C is wrong; in BC, CPAP is contraindicated with a systolic under ninety or a traumatic cause. D is wrong; a systolic of eighty is not compensated.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。脊髓损伤后出现低血压、脉搏慢、皮肤温暖干燥，是典型的神经源性休克：血管失去张力、大面积扩张，所以补液常常纠正不了。但仍要找隐匿性出血，因为创伤病人可能两者都有。A 忽略了慢脉和温暖的皮肤；C 错，在 BC，收缩压低于九十或创伤原因都是 CPAP 的禁忌；D 错，收缩压八十已经不是代偿期。

slides.title: Three lines of defence
slides.body:
Barriers: skin, cilia, stomach acid→Inflammation: many white cells→Immune response: lymphocytes only
  • Neutrophils (55–70%): first to arrive, eat bacteria
  • Eosinophils: allergy; can cause severe bronchospasm
  • Mast cells and basophils: hold histamine
  • Macrophages clean up; B and T cells target one invader, with memory
slides.say: Now the body's defences. There are three lines. First, barriers: skin, the hairs and cilia in the airway, and stomach acid. Second, inflammation, which uses many kinds of white blood cells. Third, the immune response, which uses only lymphocytes. Neutrophils are the most common white cells, fifty-five to seventy percent, and they arrive first to swallow bacteria. Eosinophils take part in allergy and can cause severe bronchospasm. Mast cells and basophils store histamine. Macrophages are the clean-up crew. B and T lymphocytes target one specific invader and remember it.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲身体的防御。共有三道防线。第一道是屏障：皮肤、气道里的鼻毛和纤毛、胃酸。第二道是炎症，用到多种白细胞。第三道是免疫反应，只靠淋巴细胞。中性粒细胞最多，占白细胞的百分之五十五到七十，最先到场吞噬细菌。嗜酸性粒细胞参与过敏，可引起严重支气管痉挛。肥大细胞和嗜碱性粒细胞储存组胺。巨噬细胞是清道夫。B 和 T 淋巴细胞专门针对某一种入侵者，而且会记住它。

slides.title: Antibodies, and who can't fight back
slides.body:
AntibodyShareJob
IgG75%most common; only one to cross the placenta
IgA15%tears, saliva, airway secretions
IgM5–10%first antibody in most infections
IgE< 1%allergy; sits on mast cells

Weak defences: newborns, older adults, diabetes, cancer, steroids, chemotherapy, HIV → infection may look mild. Infant < 3 months with temperature > 38°C: many experts advise admission.
slides.say: B cells make antibodies, and four classes matter most. IgG is about seventy-five percent, and it's the only one that crosses the placenta, protecting babies in their first months. IgA, fifteen percent, guards tears, saliva and the airway. IgM, five to ten percent, is the first antibody made in most infections. IgE is under one percent but drives allergy, because it sits on mast cells. Newborns, older adults, and people with diabetes, cancer, steroids, chemotherapy or HIV have weak defences, so their infections can look mild until they're very sick. For an infant under three months with a temperature over thirty-eight, many experts advise hospital admission.
slides.sayZh: B 细胞产生抗体，最重要的有四类。IgG 约占百分之七十五，是唯一能通过胎盘的抗体，在婴儿出生后头几个月保护他们。IgA 占百分之十五，守护泪液、唾液和气道。IgM 占百分之五到十，是大多数感染中最先产生的抗体。IgE 不到百分之一，却主导过敏，因为它挂在肥大细胞上。新生儿、老人，以及有糖尿病、癌症、用激素、做化疗或感染 HIV 的人防御力弱，感染看起来可能很轻，直到病得很重。三个月以下婴儿体温超过三十八度，许多专家主张住院。

slides.title: Inflammation: the chemicals behind it
slides.body:
• Vessels widen and leak → redness, heat, swelling, pain
  • Histamine: stored ready in mast cells, so it acts first
  • Leukotrienes: slower; tighten airways, add mucus
  • Prostaglandins: inflammation and pain
Your drugWorks against
Diphenhydramine (PCP)the histamine response
ASA, ibuprofenprostaglandin production
slides.say: Inflammation is the body's response to infection or injury. Small vessels widen and leak, giving redness, heat, swelling and pain. Mast cells drive much of this with chemicals. Histamine is stored ready inside them, so it acts first: it widens and leaks vessels and can tighten the airways. Leukotrienes come a little later; they also tighten airways and add mucus. Prostaglandins add inflammation and pain. Some of your drugs aim at these chemicals. Diphenhydramine, a PCP drug, limits the histamine response. ASA and ibuprofen block prostaglandin production, which is why they ease pain and inflammation. Knowing the target helps you predict what a drug can and can't do.
slides.sayZh: 炎症是身体对感染或损伤的反应：小血管扩张、渗漏，出现红、热、肿、痛。这主要由肥大细胞释放的化学物质驱动。组胺预先储存在肥大细胞里，所以最先起作用：让血管扩张渗漏，还能收紧气道。白三烯稍晚出现，同样收紧气道、增加黏液。前列腺素加重炎症和疼痛。你的一些药就是针对这些化学物质的：苯海拉明是 PCP 药物，能限制组胺反应；阿司匹林和布洛芬阻断前列腺素的生成，所以能缓解疼痛和炎症。知道药物的靶点，就能预判它能做什么、不能做什么。

slides.title: Four types of hypersensitivity
slides.body:
TypeDriven byTimingExample
IIgE on mast cellsseconds–minutesanaphylaxis, hives
IIIgG/IgM destroy cellshourstransfusion reaction
IIIimmune complexeshoursserum sickness
IVT cellshours–dayspoison ivy, TB skin test

Types II and III don't involve histamine. Type I is the fast one you treat with epinephrine.
slides.say: Hypersensitivity means the immune system overreacts. There are four types. Type one is immediate, within seconds to minutes. It runs on IgE stuck to mast cells, as in hives or anaphylaxis. Type two destroys cells directly with IgG or IgM antibodies; a transfusion reaction is the classic example. Type three forms antibody and antigen clumps that lodge in tissues such as the kidney, as in serum sickness. Types two and three don't involve histamine and develop over hours. Type four is delayed and run by T cells, as in a poison ivy rash or the tuberculosis skin test. On the road, type one is your big worry, because it can kill within minutes.
slides.sayZh: 超敏反应就是免疫系统反应过度，共分四型。Ⅰ型是速发的，几秒到几分钟内出现，靠挂在肥大细胞上的 IgE，比如荨麻疹或过敏性休克。Ⅱ型由 IgG 或 IgM 抗体直接破坏细胞，典型例子是输血反应。Ⅲ型形成抗原抗体复合物，沉积在肾脏等组织，比如血清病。Ⅱ型和Ⅲ型不靠组胺，在几小时内出现。Ⅳ型是迟发的，由 T 细胞介导，比如毒葛皮疹或结核菌素皮试。出车时你最该担心的是Ⅰ型，因为它几分钟内就能致命。

slides.title: Type I: from first contact to anaphylaxis
slides.body:
1st contact: IgE coats mast cells→next contact: allergen links the IgE→mast cells burst: histamine
  • Histamine triggers more histamine release
  • Vessels widen and leak → distributive shock, airway swelling
  • Severity can't be predicted; a past severe reaction raises risk
  • Treat every IgE reaction as possibly life-threatening
slides.say: Let's zoom in on type one. The first contact with an allergen usually causes no reaction; it sensitizes the patient. IgE antibodies attach to mast cells and wait, like loaded traps. On the next contact, the allergen links those antibodies, and the mast cells burst open, releasing histamine and other chemicals, which trigger even more release. Vessels widen and leak, so fluid moves out of the blood into the tissues. That causes distributive shock, and swelling that can close the upper airway. You can't predict how bad a reaction will be, and a past severe reaction raises the risk. So treat every IgE reaction as possibly life-threatening.
slides.sayZh: 放大看Ⅰ型。第一次接触过敏原通常没有反应，只是让病人致敏：IgE 抗体挂到肥大细胞上待命，像上了膛的捕兽夹。再次接触时，过敏原把这些抗体连起来，肥大细胞破裂，释放组胺等化学物质，又引发更多释放。血管扩张渗漏，液体从血液跑进组织，造成分布性休克，肿胀还可能堵住上气道。反应会有多严重无法预测，既往有严重反应的人风险更高。所以任何 IgE 反应都要当作可能致命来处理。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A man stung by a wasp got IM epinephrine 5 minutes ago. He still has a BP of 82/50 and is wheezing. What do you add?
options: IV, fluid bolus 20 mL/kg (max 2 L), then salbutamol for the wheeze
Sit him up and walk him to the ambulance
Diphenhydramine instead of any more epinephrine
Hold all fluids, because he is wheezing
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A man stung by a wasp got intramuscular epinephrine five minutes ago. He still has a blood pressure of eighty-two over fifty, and he's wheezing. What do you add? A, an IV, a fluid bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, then salbutamol for the wheeze. B, sit him up and walk him to the ambulance. C, diphenhydramine instead of any more epinephrine. D, hold all fluids, because he is wheezing. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名男子被黄蜂蜇伤，五分钟前已肌注肾上腺素，现在血压仍是八十二比五十，还在喘鸣。你要加做什么？A，开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升推注补液、最多两升，再用沙丁胺醇治喘鸣；B，扶他坐起来，走到救护车上；C，用苯海拉明代替后续的肾上腺素；D，因为他在喘鸣，所以完全不补液。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. In the BC anaphylaxis protocol, if the patient stays hypotensive, the PCP adds vascular access and a bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and treats bronchospasm with salbutamol after epinephrine. B is dangerous; keep the patient supine and never walk them. C is wrong; diphenhydramine is an add-on, not a replacement, and epinephrine can be repeated every five minutes. D is wrong; this wheeze is bronchospasm, not fluid overload, and the low pressure needs volume.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。BC 过敏性休克流程规定，病人持续低血压时，PCP 加开静脉通路，按每公斤二十毫升推注、最多两升、每五百毫升复评，并在肾上腺素之后用沙丁胺醇治疗支气管痉挛。B 很危险，病人要平卧，绝不能让他走路；C 错，苯海拉明是辅助用药，不能替代肾上腺素，而肾上腺素可以每五分钟重复；D 错，这里的喘鸣是支气管痉挛，不是液体过多，低血压需要补充容量。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the BC anaphylaxis protocol
slides.body:
Use it for: signs of anaphylaxis + allergen exposure + unstable (fainting, ↓ LOC, BP < 90, or breathing distress)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Supine; don't walk the patient
  • Remove the allergen (stinger, stop the drug)
  • Airway; oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Epinephrine IM
  • Transport; continue care en route

PCP adds

  • IV + fluid if still hypotensive or poorly perfused
  • 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Salbutamol for bronchospasm, after epinephrine
  • Diphenhydramine to limit the histamine response

Book: epinephrine by auto-injector, SC or IM. BC: IM only.
slides.say: Use the BC anaphylaxis protocol when there are signs of anaphylaxis, exposure to an allergen, and the patient is unstable: fainting, a decreased level of consciousness, a systolic under ninety, or breathing distress. The left column is what you already do as an EMR: lay the patient flat and don't walk them, remove the allergen, give oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, give intramuscular epinephrine, and transport. The right column is new. If the patient stays hypotensive or poorly perfused, the PCP starts an IV and gives twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. Then salbutamol for bronchospasm, and diphenhydramine. Remember: BC epinephrine is intramuscular only.
slides.sayZh: BC 过敏性休克流程的适用条件：有过敏性休克的征象、接触过过敏原，而且病人不稳定——晕厥、意识水平下降、收缩压低于九十或呼吸窘迫。左栏是你作为 EMR 本来就做的：让病人平卧、不要让他走路，去除过敏原，给氧使血氧达到九十四以上，肌注肾上腺素，转运。右栏是新的：如果病人仍然低血压或灌注不良，PCP 开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升补液，最多两升，每五百毫升复评；然后用沙丁胺醇治支气管痉挛，再给苯海拉明。记住：BC 的肾上腺素只能肌注。

slides.title: Stress and disease
slides.body:
Alarmcatecholamines: fight or flightcan weaken immunity
Resistancecortisol, aldosteroneglucose ↑, BP held, sodium kept
Exhaustionadrenal glands depletedglucose ↓, immunity down

Long-term stress → weaker immunity and clogged arteries → heart attack, stroke. This applies to you, too.
slides.say: Stress, physical or emotional, triggers a three-stage response called the general adaptation syndrome. In the alarm stage, catecholamines like epinephrine prepare the body for fight or flight, but they can also weaken immunity. In the resistance stage, cortisol raises the blood glucose and helps hold the blood pressure, while aldosterone keeps sodium. If stress goes on too long, the body reaches exhaustion: the adrenal glands are depleted, glucose falls and immunity drops. On scene, this means a critically ill patient may have a high glucose from stress, or a low one after a long struggle, so always measure it. And chronic stress hurts paramedics too.
slides.sayZh: 应激，无论是身体上的还是情绪上的，会触发一个三阶段反应，叫一般适应综合征。警觉期，肾上腺素等儿茶酚胺让身体准备战斗或逃跑，但也可能削弱免疫。抵抗期，皮质醇升高血糖、帮助维持血压，醛固酮保留钠。应激持续太久，身体进入衰竭期：肾上腺耗竭，血糖下降，免疫力下降。在现场，这意味着危重病人可能因应激而血糖高，也可能在长时间挣扎后血糖低，所以一定要测。慢性应激对救护员自己也有伤害。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Name the shock type before you bolus: fluid fixes volume, not pumps
  • Neurogenic shock: low BP, slow pulse; fluid may not fix it
  • BC: no CPAP if systolic < 90 or the cause is trauma
  • Anaphylaxis: epinephrine first; salbutamol, diphenhydramine are add-ons
  • Weak immunity (older, steroids, chemo): infection can hide
  • Measure glucose: BGL < 4.0 → PCP can give D10W IV
slides.say: New watch-outs. First, name the shock type before you give fluid: a bolus refills an empty tank, but it can't fix a failing pump or a blocked pipe. Second, neurogenic shock gives low pressure with a slow pulse, and fluid may not fix it. Third, in BC, CPAP is not used with a systolic under ninety or a traumatic cause. Fourth, in anaphylaxis, epinephrine always comes first; salbutamol and diphenhydramine are add-ons. Fifth, patients with weak immunity can hide a serious infection. And sixth, stress can push glucose up or down, so measure it. If it's under four, the PCP can give D10W through an IV.
slides.sayZh: 新的注意事项。第一，补液前先分清休克类型：推注补液能加满空油箱，却修不好衰竭的泵，也通不了堵住的管道。第二，神经源性休克是低血压配慢脉，补液可能纠正不了。第三，在 BC，收缩压低于九十或创伤原因不用 CPAP。第四，过敏性休克永远先给肾上腺素，沙丁胺醇和苯海拉明只是辅助。第五，免疫力弱的病人可能把严重感染藏起来。第六，应激可以让血糖升高也可以让它下降，所以一定要测；低于四，PCP 可以经静脉给 D10W。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Shock starves cells → lactic acid; name the type before you give fluid
  2. Type I allergy = IgE + mast cells + histamine; can turn deadly in minutes
  3. Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine first; PCP adds IV fluid, salbutamol, diphenhydramine

Next: Chapter 7, Pharmacology
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: shock starves cells of oxygen, so they make lactic acid and fail; name the type of shock before you decide on fluid. Two: a type one allergy runs on IgE, mast cells and histamine, and it can turn deadly in minutes. Three: in anaphylaxis, intramuscular epinephrine always comes first; the PCP then adds IV fluid if the patient stays hypotensive, salbutamol for bronchospasm, and diphenhydramine. Next, we start Chapter 7, pharmacology, and look at how the drugs you now carry actually work. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，休克让细胞缺氧，细胞产生乳酸并衰竭；决定补液前先分清休克类型。二，Ⅰ型过敏靠 IgE、肥大细胞和组胺，几分钟内就可能致命。三，过敏性休克永远先肌注肾上腺素；PCP 再加上：持续低血压时静脉补液、沙丁胺醇治支气管痉挛、苯海拉明。下节课进入第七章药理学，看看你现在携带的药物到底怎么起作用。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
